subject: research/simdesign-shellorder
professional: a senior FE analyst in structural stability doing solution verification (Roache / ASME V&V 20 practice) on a linear buckling model; first checks: that the levels reproduce, the order and extrapolation arithmetic, whether three levels are in the asymptotic range (GCI and its ratio check), whether the solver recovers a textbook case (Euler column), and whether the closed form compared against is the right one for a short clamped bar

evidence.correctness: Run in a scratch copy (scratchpad/shellorder/copy; /usr/bin/python3.13, scikit-fem 12.0.2, scipy 1.18.1). `python experiments/scan.py` re-run end to end (the README says it never was): levels 0 and 1 reproduce scan.txt to every printed digit (10021.552, 9686.543 N), level 2 too (9629.962 N in 322 s); analyze.py then rewrites summary.txt identically. Independent script scratchpad/shellorder/indep.py (not the author's analyze.py): closed form 4.013 sqrt(E Iy G J)/l^2 = 8460.649 N (Timoshenko and Gere cantilever, tip load at centroid); with the exact Saint-Venant series J (Timoshenko and Goodier) instead of the 0.63 approximation 8460.342 N, so the J approximation costs 0.004%; d1/d2 = 5.921, p = 2.5658, Richardson limit 9618.464 N, ratio 1.1368, fine level 0.120% above the limit: all match summary.txt and the README. Roache's GCI_fine (Fs 1.25) = 0.149%, so the 14% gap is far outside the discretisation band even under assumed p = 2 (limit 9611.1) or p = 4 (9626.2). Solver check against a textbook case: axial Euler column l = 80, 40x2x1 mesh gives 413.86 N vs pi^2 E Iy/(4 l^2) = 411.23 N (ratio 1.0064). Slenderness trend (author's engine, my sweep.py): at the 12x4x2-equivalent mesh FE/closed form is 1.145, 1.074, 1.038 for l/w = 3, 6, 12, so the gap does close with slenderness as the README hypothesises.
evidence.completeness: Claimed: three uniform levels (6x2x1, 12x4x2, 24x8x4) solved, analyze.py computes order and Richardson limit, 1 test, README/research index entry. All present and working: scan.py re-run reproduces scan.txt, analyze.py reproduces summary.txt, the test passes, research/README.md:568 lists it. Runtime claims: test 24 s here (README 'about 40 s'), fine solve 322 s on this machine (README about 13 min). Live page https://marisstella.app/research/simdesign-shellorder/ not reachable from this session (curl status 000), not counted against it. Weak spot: `scan.py 2` (the documented per-level usage) overwrites scan.txt with only that level, after which analyze.py fails on f[1]/f[2].
evidence.verification: `cd research/simdesign-shellorder && python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 1 passed in 23.6 s. The one test checks only that the 12x4x2 load is below the 6x2x1 load and above half of it. Four seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py, all survived: shear traction doubled (eigbuckle.py:42, halves every critical load), shear modulus term halved in the prebuckling stress (eigbuckle.py:54), closed-form coefficient 4.013 -> 3.013 (eigbuckle.py:87), Richardson sign flipped in analyze.py:12. No test pins an FE output to a textbook value, the closed form to a number, or analyze.py to scan.txt.
evidence.craft: Read eigbuckle.py, scan.py, analyze.py, test_scan.py. Small and readable, numbers written from code. Defects: eigbuckle.py is byte-identical to research/simdesign-shellconverge's (copied engine, and copied again into simdesign-shellaspect); the module docstring calls ElementHex2 'serendipity' but in scikit-fem it is the 27-node triquadratic element (ElementHexS2 is the 20-node serendipity one), which matters for the expected convergence order the README discusses; scan.py with level arguments writes a partial scan.txt that analyze.py then cannot read; analyze.py has no guard for fewer than three rows; files opened without close (minor).
evidence.claims: Backed by files and my reruns: the three loads and ratios (scan.txt, reproduced), differences 335.0 and 56.6, p 2.57, limit 9618.5 N, ratio 1.137, 0.12% (summary.txt, recomputed independently), 'the gap is not a discretisation error' (GCI 0.15% vs a 14% gap), AI-assistance and 'stylised, preliminary' notes, limitations (one triple, clamp singularity untreated). The attribution of the gap to shear deformation and warping restraint is labelled a hypothesis. Small gaps: the README describes the expected order loosely ('between the 2 and 4 one might expect') without naming the eigenvalue rate O(h^{2k}) for degree-k elements (Babuska-Osborn), and 'scan.py itself was not re-run end to end' is now outdated in the good direction (it reproduces). README runtime '1 test, about 40 s' is 24 s here.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on it: the numbers reproduce and simdesign-shellaspect already took its l/w next step. Nearest prior work: Roache 1998 (cited) and its GCI procedure (Roache 1994 J. Fluids Eng.; Celik et al. 2008 J. Fluids Eng. 130, 078001), ASME V&V 20-2009; eigenvalue a priori rates (Babuska and Osborn, Handbook of Numerical Analysis II, 1991); lateral-torsional buckling with warping restraint and pre-buckling deformation (Timoshenko and Gere ch. 6 tabulated cantilever coefficients; Trahair, Flexural-Torsional Buckling of Structures, 1993). Against that the result is a routine solution-verification step, not a new finding, and the README does not claim novelty. It is sound as far as it goes: one triple, no GCI, no asymptotic-ratio check, no fourth level, and the question it opens (why 14%) is left to a hypothesis.
evidence.domain: Matches practice: uniform refinement ratio 2 in all directions, observed order and Richardson limit, clear statement that three points cannot confirm the order. Departs: Roache is cited but the GCI with a safety factor and the asymptotic-range check are not reported; the observed order 2.57 is not set against the expected O(h^4) eigenvalue rate for quadratic elements, nor is the clamp-edge singularity probed (e.g. graded mesh at x = 0); the comparator 4.013 is the zero-warping limit, while this short clamped bar has a warping parameter sqrt(pi^2 E Cw/(G J l^2)) = 0.27 (my indep.py, Cw = w^3 b^3/144) where a practitioner would use the warping-dependent cantilever coefficient, and the well-known pre-buckling (in-plane curvature) factor 1/sqrt((1-Iy/Iz)(1-GJ/EIz)) = 1.077 for this section is not mentioned among candidate causes of the 14% gap.

defects.what: One test, checking only that the 12x4x2 load is below the 6x2x1 load and above half of it; all four seeded mutants survive (traction doubled, prebuckling stress shear term halved, closed-form coefficient changed, Richardson sign flipped). No test pins the engine to a textbook case (Euler column recovers to 0.6%), the closed form to a number, or analyze.py to scan.txt.

The 14% gap is attributed to shear deformation and warping restraint without a number, while the comparator is the zero-warping 4.013 coefficient although the bar's warping parameter is 0.27, and the standard pre-buckling curvature factor (1.077 for this section, Trahair 1993) is not named as a candidate; the warping-dependent tabulated cantilever coefficient would be the practitioner's comparator. No lateral-torsional buckling prior work beyond the slender-beam formula is cited.

Roache is cited but no GCI or asymptotic-range check is reported, and the observed order 2.57 is not set against the O(h^4) eigenvalue rate expected for quadratic elements (Babuska-Osborn); the clamp-edge singularity is not probed with a graded mesh, so one triple carries the whole order estimate.

Docstring calls ElementHex2 a serendipity element; in scikit-fem it is the 27-node triquadratic element (ElementHexS2 is serendipity), the kind of detail that matters when reasoning about the expected convergence order.

The documented per-level usage `scan.py [level ...]` overwrites scan.txt with only the requested levels, after which analyze.py fails indexing f[1]/f[2]; nobody can resume or re-run the 13-minute level alone without losing the table.
Copied engine: eigbuckle.py is byte-identical to research/simdesign-shellconverge's and copied again into simdesign-shellaspect, instead of importing one shared module.

verdict: Small, honest and reproducible: re-running scan.py end to end reproduces all three loads in scan.txt to the printed digit, my own script reproduces the order 2.566, the Richardson limit 9618.46 N and the 0.12% fine-level error, the closed form recomputes to 8460.649 N, the engine recovers an Euler column to 0.6%, and a slenderness sweep confirms the gap shrinks (1.145, 1.074, 1.038 at l/w = 3, 6, 12). GCI is 0.15%, so 'not a discretisation error' holds. It does not meet the bar: one test that catches none of four seeded mutants, and the method stops short of what a stability analyst would do with the result (no GCI or asymptotic check, the 2.57 order unexplained against the expected O(h^4), a zero-warping comparator for a bar with warping parameter 0.27, the pre-buckling factor unmentioned). A routine verification step, not new, and it does not claim to be.
